newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker with U.S. treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker with U.S. treasuries.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended weaker on Wednesday after U.S. economic data released earlier today overshadowed a Canadian two-year bond auction.

"Anticipation of the Fed's Beige Book economic summary cast a long shadow over the markets and wrinkled interest in Canada's two-year bond auction," Technical Data analyst Jeoff Hall said in a report.

Canada's 30-year benchmark bond lost C$0.32 to C$110.38 to yield 7.119 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark, which fell 11/32 to yield 6.88 percent. The spread between the two narrowed to 24 basis points from 25 basis points on Tuesday.

The U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book report for March said the U.S. economy continues to plough ahead with scant sign of any inflationary pressures. Wage gains remained moderate despite tight labor markets, the report said.

Before the report was released, Canada issued results of its C$3.0 billion, two-year bond auction with C$1.8 billion in new cash. The 4.0 percent bonds produced an average yield of 4.447 percent at a price of C$99.156.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.00 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.17 to C$103.68 yielding 6.481 percent, while the U.S. 10-year dipped 6/32 to yield 6.61 percent.
The negative spread widened to 13 basis points from 12 basis points.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.01 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.20 percent.
